timeline.draft_answer: In October 2018, ETH Zurich was one of the first universities to receive official accreditation under the Swiss Higher Education Act, which had entered into force in 2015. The act requires all public and private institutions wishing to use the designation "university," "university of applied sciences," or "university of teacher education" to be accredited every seven years. The accreditation is awarded by the Swiss Accreditation Council, made up of twenty independent members including representatives from the world of work, higher education institutions, students, non-professional teaching staff, and academic staff. As part of this process, ETH updated its "Guidelines for the internal quality assurance system" and supplemented them with a list of functions responsible for various aspects. Rector Sarah Springman also highlighted teaching initiatives such as ETH Talent, aimed at strengthening interdisciplinary skills across all levels, and noted that more departments were introducing a split in first-year examinations. The evidence does not describe a broader institutional "reorganization" beyond these accreditation-related quality assurance updates.
